answer: A hydrodynamic protocol limits Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to local marine pressure data. A verifier challenges an agent to stream hydrostatic nonces as the ocean tide ebbs across a raven basalt reef, verifying them across the decentralized node nebula. An attacker must incur the capital cost of deploying discrete marine sensors rather than virtualizing identities. However, storm surges can distort pressure baselines, falsely rejecting authentic agents.
